issues.legal_issue: A decree enforcing a charge against property held under occupancy rights is not barred by a statutory restriction that was no longer in force when the decree was passed.
material_facts: The purchaser covenanted that unpaid purchase money would be a charge on the property and took possession of it as an occupancy tenant.

The trial court refused to enforce the charge because of the property's occupancy status, but the restriction on decrees for sale or foreclosure of occupancy rights had been repealed before the decree was passed.
The High Court granted a decree enforcing the charge.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to hold that the charge could be enforced against the property because the statutory prohibition had been repealed before the decree was passed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act, 1920, contained a prohibition on decrees for sale or foreclosure of an occupancy tenant's rights, but it had been repealed before the decree was passed. The repealed prohibition therefore did not prevent a decree enforcing the charge.

predicates.charge_enforcement_suit: A claimant brought a suit seeking to enforce a charge against property.
predicates.property_held_as_occupancy_tenancy: The property against which the charge was sought was held by the opposing party under occupancy rights.
predicates.restriction_absent_when_decree_passed: The restriction that would have barred a decree against occupancy rights was no longer in force when the decree was passed.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks enforcement of a charge against property held under occupancy rights and the relevant restriction is absent when the decree is passed, the court may enforce the charge against the property.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may grant a claimant relief enforcing a charge even though the claimant did not appeal the trial court's refusal of that relief.
material_facts: The sale agreement provided that unpaid purchase money would be a charge on the property.
The trial court refused to grant relief enforcing the charge.
The claimant did not appeal that refusal, while the purchaser appealed the trial court's decree.
The High Court granted relief enforcing the charge in the purchaser's appeal.
issues.conclusion: The claimant's failure to appeal did not bar the High Court from granting a decree enforcing the charge in her favour.
issues.legal_principle: Order XLI, Rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers an appellate court to pass a decree that ought in law to have been passed, or such further or other decree as the case requires, in favour of a party who has not appealed. The Court relied on Radhika Mohan v. Sudhir Chandra, A.I.R. 1937 Calcutta 10, and Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal, [1969] 3 S.C.R. 944; the latter explains that a decree that 'ought to have been passed' is one that ought in law to have been passed, and that the power may be used as the justice of the case requires.

rule.if: appeal_from_trial_decree and trial_court_denied_charge_enforcement and claimant_did_not_appeal and sale_agreement_secured_unpaid_price_by_charge

predicates.appeal_from_trial_decree: A party appealed from a trial court's decree.
predicates.trial_court_denied_charge_enforcement: The trial court refused the claimant's request to enforce a charge against property.
predicates.claimant_did_not_appeal: The claimant did not appeal the trial court's refusal of the requested relief.
predicates.sale_agreement_secured_unpaid_price_by_c: The sale agreement provided that unpaid purchase money would be secured by a charge on the property.

issues.definition: When a party appeals from a decree, the trial court denied charge enforcement, the claimant did not appeal, and the sale agreement secured unpaid purchase money by a charge, the appellate court may grant charge relief to the non-appealing claimant.
